core_obligations: Derive the dimension bounds from the dimension base change lemma, and reduce part (1) to part (2) by applying part (2) to the structure sheaf O_Z, whose base change is O_{Z'} (proof lines 15216-15220).

Check that F' is coherent: F is of finite type since X is locally Noetherian, a pullback of a finite type module is of finite type, and on a locally Noetherian scheme finite type implies coherent (proof lines 15223-15228).

Prove the cycle identity coefficient by coefficient: for an integral W of delta-dimension k and an integral W' of delta'-dimension k + c mapping into W, with generic points xi, xi' and local rings A, B, use F'_{xi'} = B tensor_A M for M = F_xi, identify the coefficient n of [W'] in g^*[F]_k as length_B(B tensor_A M) and the coefficient m in [F']_{k+c} as length_A(M) length_B(B/m_AB), and conclude with the algebra lemma on the length of a pullback (proof lines 15229-15251).
proof_roadmap: Dimensions and the reduction of part (1) to part (2) (proof lines 15216-15220).
Coherence of the base changed sheaf (proof lines 15223-15228).
Coefficient comparison at the generic points and the algebra lemma on pullbacks (proof lines 15229-15251).
difficulty_reason: In the base change situation for the cycle theory, the lemma states two things: for a closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension at most k with base change Z', the delta'-dimension of Z' is at most k + c and [Z']_{k+c} = g^*[Z]_k, and for a coherent sheaf F whose support has delta-dimension at most k the base change F' has support of delta'-dimension at most k + c and g^*[F]_k = [F']_{k+c} (statement lines 15192-15208). The proof reduces the dimension claims to the dimension base change lemma, deduces part (1) from part (2) by applying part (2) to O_Z, whose base change is O_{Z'}, and then proves part (2) coefficient by coefficient: for an integral closed subscheme W of delta-dimension k and an integral W' of delta'-dimension k + c mapping into W, with generic points xi and xi' and local rings A and B, one has F'_{xi'} = B tensor_A M for M = F_xi, so the coefficient of [W'] in g^*[F]_k is length_B(B tensor_A M) while the coefficient in [F']_{k+c} is length_A(M) length_B(B/m_AB), and the two agree by the algebra lemma on the length of a pullback module (proof lines 15210-15251). The reduction of the sheaf statement to a coefficient identity of lengths of a pullback is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
